Term1: Bacterial meningitis with gram-negative diplococci suggesting neisseria meningitidis
Text:
# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH GRAM-NEGATIVE DIPLOCOCCI SUGGESTING NEISSERIA MENINGITIDIS

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible after obtaining blood cultures and performing a lumbar puncture to obtain cerebrospinal fluid. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

If meningococcal meningitis is identified, antimicrobial prophylaxis should be considered for close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for advice and assistance.

# Consult Infectious Diseases
